title: Ubiquiti Unifi Cloud Gateway Ultra $179 Delivered / C&C / in-Store @ Centre Com
body:
Deal: Ubiquiti Unifi Cloud Gateway Ultra $179 Delivered / C&C / in-Store @ Centre Com

[mrpenpengendo] Fantastic little device for top-speed NBN FTTP plans. Just be aware it only runs Unifi Network application and doesn't have Unifi Protect or the other apps.
[Referenced] I've got one, works well, just keep in mind although the WAN port is 2.5gig the rest of the ports are only 1gig. Software is a bit limited if you're used to opnsense or something but its good enough for me
[JoeBogan] I don’t even what this thing is and does so I’m gonna do a rare ozbargain and not buy it
[xjcs88] Before using Ubiquiti I always thought Asus routers are the best T-T
[PeelThis] Ubquitis are slick, I like their APs for wireless but prefer mikrotik routers but 'best' is subjective to what you're trying to do with it.
[Techefy] Oh ohh cloud gateway — i have other means
[ashanrath] What's the Ubiquiti environment like these days vs openwrt?
[xjcs88] I feel like macOS VS Linux.
Both nice stuff just pick your side.
[noren7] I really like this description.
One benefit I really like of the Ubiquiti is the stupid easy to enable IDS/IPS. But most people won't care about this or arguably even need it
[noisymime] Ubiquiti really is more about buying into an ecosystem than just a single product and their real value is in how well they all tie together. Being able to manage your router, your APs, your switches, your security cameras etc all through a single dashboard is pretty slick. It's even better if you have to manage multiple sites.
[cougielah] I have this and had to turn off a bunch of monitoring and filtering features (on by default) because it falls over (overloaded) specifically on Google Meet. Agree it is a fantastic little thing but at that price point there are limitations.
[LanceVance] Does this include Wi-Fi? I've always found Ubiquiti's product descriptions confusing.
[happychappy1] This is a router with a built in switch. No WiFi. To get one with WiFi all in one, you want a Dream Router 7 or Express 7.
[Earl of Lemongrab] You'll need to combine this with an AP
https://www.mwave.com.au/products/ubiquiti-networks-u6-plus-…
[chrismheath] Which will need a PoE injector as the Cloud Gateway doesnt have PoE. Its probably my only real complaint about this product, I'd assume almost everyone at this price point may only need this + a u6/equivalent if they don't have many accessible wired devices (therefore no need for a switch).
[theUnderdog] Damn just bought a UX7. Should have waited for this ine instead
[Domingo] Every time this goes up I wonder if I should upgrade my Edgerouter X to this so all my Ubiquiti devices are on the same platform, but it never quite seems worth it.
[Ooops] Comes with privacy invasion features unfortunately :(
https://www.ui.com/legal/privacypolicy/
Information Collected By Us. In general, we collect certain information by which someone could personally identify you or individuals that you allow to use or access the Services (" Personally Identifiable Information"….
How We May Disclose Information. We may disclose the information we collect related to the Services as follows:
Usage Data. We may provide Usage Data to our customers in conne
Additionally, if you discontinue using our Services or update your account information, we may retain the data previously collected about you.
[bozzonac] https://help.ui.com/hc/en-us/articles/360042384093-Analytics…
I have the UCG-Max and there's an user setting that allows you to choose what level of information you share back with them for analytics (Standard, Minimal, Off).
[mahdoo] They've ignored these user controlled settings in the past.
Insane that people are downvoting this. Ubiquiti had a MASSIVE privacy scandal a few years back. Are peoples memories really this short-term?
[netsurfer] Ubiquiti has no AU store (so Ubiquiti doesn't collect our physical address). Furthermore, who says we have to use our main email address to signup? So if you sign up as Luke Skywalker and that get exposed, that's a big deal?
[mahdoo] @netsurfer: You are forgetting these are cloud connected routers that have security features on them that allow for decrypting of all network traffic.
No one is talking about billing information lol. We're talking about your internet traffic, and network patterns.
You need to really trust a company and their practices to trust them with this level of access. And ubiquiti has broken that trust on numerous occasions, and proven themselves to not be worthy of your trust.
Their tech is cool, but your data is not safe with them.
https://www.cybereason.com/blog/whistleblower-accuses-ubiqui…
https://www.theregister.com/on-prem/2019/11/07/sure-we-made-…
[netsurfer] @mahdoo: Did you read the article and fully understand it? If yes, you can't think of a way to protect against that? There is 2 factor authentication and disable cloud remote management.
If you want to go down SDN path, what are the other choices? TP-Link Omada? Frankly, Google scans all our emails, I reckon Microsoft does the same, same goes for Apple. Our government has records of all our transactions (from the banks). OZB logs my IP address (it is in the terms and conditions) and knows who I work for.
P.S. I don't neg votes.
[mahdoo] @netsurfer: You learn a lot about a company from how they respond to these incidents.
Ubiquiti handled both situations through lies and misleading their customers.
Can't get more clearer than that. Do what you think is best, but I cannot in good faith suggest anyone touch their products.
[netsurfer] @mahdoo: First article - if you think this only happens to Ubiquiti, then you have a more serious problem.
Second one - you can opt out of it.
So, if Asus, Netgear, TP-Link, Ubiquiti all had reported issues, what exactly is left? OpenWRT and OPNSense?
With Ubiquiti, you can easily put all your surveillance cameras in its own VLAN. IoT is its own VLANs (do you REALLY trust all those cheap IoT devices to mix them with your network)? You can get your phones and PC to discover those IoT devices and interact with them BUT those IoT devices cannot establish connections to your trusted network if you put them in a separate VLAN. Those things are already considered. Try doing that with an Asus routers, the VLAN support is so poor.
You can have family members able to only look at cameras, but cannot alter settings. The key is to learn from what happened and actually do something about it.
[netsurfer] @mahdoo: From what I gathered, you can setup your own local UniFi controller server and not use UniFi's cloud. With that setup, you don't store anything on UniFi's cloud servers.
Honestly though, one of my issues with UniFi is its config cloud backup is not reliable. It was so annoying that I was glad I didn't put all eggs in one basket. When UniFi works, it is great, but when it doesn't work, it can be a real pain to troubleshoot. The network diagram UniFi draws for my network is wrong. It can't figure out the flow to and from 3rd party gears.
[mahdoo] @netsurfer:
With that setup, you don't store anything on UniFi's cloud servers.
Local controllers still send significant analytics - You have to manually block ubiquiti's domains, and better off not providing the VM or container running the controller internet access at all.
Though my understanding is that the Cloud Gateways are designed to not use the local controllers (or cloudkeys) and run the management software locally on device. It'd be more complicated to control what data this sends, considering that it's designed to be your edge. Ubiquiti have been attempting to enforce cloud accounts recently as well.
Anywho - sorry not replying to all your other messages. Do what you want, I'm not here to control what you do. I wouldn't suggest any SDN or app based network management. It's likely the others are just as bad privacy wise - but they haven't been as vocal about their lack of giving a shit as Ubiquiti have.
If you really want fancy networking at home, you're better off with something like OPNsense/pfSense/OpenWRT. Combine with home assistant for the other things.
[netsurfer] @mahdoo: You wouldn't buy this if you go local controller. Frankly, this one isn't worth buying (because their current gen controllers are better, WiFi 7 without 10Gbps LAN doesn't make sense, with NBN supporting 2Gbps, single 2.5Gbps doesn't make sense either).
It's not just SDN, you cannot use any current mobile apps for your routers (because those essentially have the same issue). Other routers have another issue, lack of firmware updates. Vulnerabilities are often left unpatched. No router company has a perfect record.
Multiple SSIDs (and no, it is not just 1 for 2.4GHz, 1 for 5GHz), VLANs, easier IoT handling when you setup multiple VLANs. Whether you like it or not, the Americans tend to do better firmware (though UniFi changes firmware far too often to be honest). You get a lot more features compared to Asus, TP-Link.
[netsurfer] @mahdoo: I use UniFi, OpenWRT, OPNsense, MikroTik. Actually, I use more than those 4 (I have products from other vendors).
Also, I don't do cloud backup for Unifi config. Last time I upgraded the controller, I used my local copy. It's wishful thinking that UniFi wants people's data so bad they would just keep using its cloud to store your stuff. Anonymous analytics data is fine (most Web sites do analytics anyway).
There are other family members which need to use UniFi mobile apps (not for network). Honestly, data collections from some other companies are more serious, but we don't do anything about them.
[Ooops] @netsurfer: They collect everything from the router and there's no possibility to opt-out unless you add another physical device between the router and the internet to block the traffic.
[netsurfer] @Ooops: Incorrect, another physical device in between doesn't solve the problem. Also, if someone knows your router config and it is game over for you, then you have a more serious problem.
The correct mindset is you CANNOT assume the router is something that's protecting you, especially with IPv6. You just need to decide whether you want the SDN trade off (and beef up your security accordingly). I know a lot of doctors use Ubiquiti setup. Also, it is naïve to think the issue you pointed out is only applicable to Ubiquiti. If you use mobile apps for your router, just because it is not Ubiquiti, it is much safer? That's wishful thinking.
[Ooops] @netsurfer: Another device aka a DNS hole.
I personally am not using any apps for my router. Also, that's because others are doing it that doesn't make it ok.
With respect to doctors, I know quite a few of them at all and none of them give 2c on your privacy or their own or have any respect for any of it. They will use whatever they can to give them an edge on the market.
[netsurfer] @Ooops: There is another way, don't use Ubiquiti cloud. You can run / host the network part of the controller locally (without using the mothership). I don't know whether Ubiquiti provided the same for Protect and Access.
However, it does defeat the purpose of getting this device.
[Ooops] @netsurfer: That's the problem. They collect and send data regardless.
[netsurfer] @Ooops: Do you actually have an Ubiquiti UniFi controller?
You don't need to auto backup your config to UniFi cloud. I don't so when I upgraded to a new controller, I had to use a local copy.
If you do have one, is your remote management turned off? If yes, what's the big deal?
I am guessing anonymous analytics data is the concern? If so, then yeah, don't buy (you could pi-hole block it, but honestly, just don't buy UniFi products).
Asus, TP-Link and Netgear… if you ended up not buying one of their popular routers, you hardly get any firmware updates.
VLANs on most routers are a pain so you end up not doing them. That's not a good solution.
Consider Amazon is so stingy with their cloud (for Ring and Blink, you need to pay), don't expect Ubiquiti to give you heaps of free storage.
[netsurfer] Ubiquiti Unifi is SDN based. It not only support network, some of their SDN controllers support surveillance cameras, access (doors), etc… Some people think of it like iOS / Mac. A big part of it is the cloud setup. It even tells you the NBN provider (if your NBN provider is more of a reseller, it actually tells you the actual infrastructure provider). The mobile app is more configurable than most traditional router apps.
Google GMail scans your emails. By using OZB, you agreed that your IP address will be logged (OZB is more concern about you doing dodgy stuff - i.e. trying to create multiple accounts).
[soulfuljyl] Does it show one or two lines??…… I see myself out….
